'''Marcus Darrell Williams''' (born [[December 3]] [[1985]] in [[Los Angeles, California]]) is a former [[college basketball]] player for the [[University of Connecticut]]. He initially declared for the [[2006 NBA Draft]] after his sophomore year [http://www.uconnhuskies.com/AllStories/MBasketball/2006/04/25/20060425.html], but decided a few days later to remain for at least one more season in college [http://www.azcentral.com/arizonarepublic/sports/articles/0428uabkc0428.html].

==Controversy==
He became the center of controversy in December 2005 when he was charged with trying to sell ten stolen laptop computers taken from dormitory rooms on the university campus. 
As of June 20, 2006, Marcus has declared for the 2006 NBA draft. He is very aware of his past incident though he has grown from  this experience. He's very apprecitive of his former Uconn coach, [[Jim Calhoun]], and family. 

==Draft==
Marcus declared for the 2006 NBA draft. He has worked out for the [[Atlanta Hawks]], and the [[Toronto Raptors]], to name a few. The [[2006 NBA Draft]] is being held on [[June 28]], 2006. He is regarded by many to be a lottery pick due to his unselfishness on the court and being a true [[point guard]].

==Personal==
He has a younger sister, Marchelle, a very potential writer and artist. His parents are Kelly & Michelle Williams.
